title: HB1598 (2020 Regular): RELATING TO FIREARMS.

provenance.fetched_by: Open States bulk data (Hawaii) (gun-policy Stage 5, Hawaii); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official Hawaii text (Introduced, official copy, https://data.capitol.hawaii.gov/sessions/session2020/bills/HB1598_.HTM; sha256 894d1f35f8697fcc7bc368cca05ce17348ac0b829f9ef44c16c00af9ded7a860)
provenance.note: Introduced text. The quoted parts are the clean sentences; the bill's core changes (attorney general may grant a statewide license to carry a pistol or revolver concealed or unconcealed, county chiefs limited to on-duty security guards, training course within 180 days before applying, fee changed from $10 to $100 paid to the State) sit in subsections that carry struck words, so they are described here and not quoted. No passage vote is recorded in the data; the text read is the bill as filed.

operative_text:
SECTION 2 (HRS 134-9): The chief of police of each county and the attorney general shall adopt procedures to require that any person granted a license to carry a concealed or unconcealed weapon on the person shall:
SECTION 2 (HRS 134-9): (2) Appear to be a suitable person to be so licensed; (3) Not be prohibited under section 134-7 from the ownership or possession of a firearm; and (4) Not have been adjudged insane or not appear to be mentally deranged.
SECTION 2 (HRS 134-9): No person shall carry concealed or unconcealed on the person a pistol or revolver without being licensed to do so under this section or in compliance with sections 134-5(c) or 134-25.
